title: Insight 'Why?' disclosure prints [object Object] and null for workload and forecast inputs
evidence: function formatInputValue(value) { if (typeof value === 'number') return value.toLocaleString('en-PH'); return String(value); }  // server: 'busiest' => ['name' => ..., 'active_tasks' => ..., 'workload_score' => ...] (DashboardInsightEngine.php:255); 'income_r_squared' => $details['income']['r_squared'] ?? null (:157); 'safe_spending_limit' => ... : null (:110)
impact: Admins and officers who open 'Why am I seeing this?' on the workload insight read 'busiest ([object Object]), freest ([object Object])'. On the forecast and budget insights they read 'income r squared (null)' or 'safe spending limit (null)'. The one explanation the card offers is unreadable.
suggested_fix: In whyItems, skip entries whose value is null or undefined. Flatten objects into readable text (for example 'busiest: Ana Cruz, 4 active tasks'), or have the server send flat, human-labelled inputs. Add a Vitest case for an object-valued input and a null input.
verifier_notes: formatInputValue only special-cases numbers; String() on the busiest/freest arrays from taskWorkloadBalance gives [object Object], and the nullable budget/forecast inputs give "null". RoleBriefing shows insights to ADMIN and SBO_OFFICER, so this is reachable.

title: Grievance classifier misses plural and inflected forms of whole-word keywords
evidence:
MEDIUM_KEYWORDS = ("broken", "delay", "missing", ...)
"Financial Integrity": ("money", "fund", "fraud*", "receipt", "budget", ..., "payment", ...)
"Academic / Faculty": ("grades", "teacher", "professor", "exam", "class", "schedule")  -- whole-word match: rf"\b{keyword}\b"
impact: I ran these through the engine. 'Our org funds and receipts are missing' is filed under General, not Financial Integrity. 'The teachers delayed releasing our grades and exams' comes out Low urgency because neither 'delay' nor 'teacher' matches. Real complaints worded naturally fall into the wrong category and urgency, and so they sort low in the SAO and Admin queues. The PHP mirror in GrievanceController.php:42-48 has the same lists and the same behaviour.
suggested_fix: Make the nouns and verbs that inflect into stems ('fund*', 'receipt*', 'payment*', 'teacher*', 'exam*', 'delay*', 'complaint*', 'room*', 'chair*', 'facilit*', 'class' plus 'classes', 'grade*') in both the Python and PHP lists. Keep AiFallbackParityTest green, and add parametrized tests for the plural phrasings above.
verifier_notes: Reproduced in the engine: "Our org funds and receipts are missing" -> Medium/General; "The teachers delayed releasing our grades and exams" -> Low (category Academic via "grades"). PHP lists in GrievanceController are identical. Minor wording: "teacher" is a category keyword only, not an urgency keyword.

title: Reviewers see the machine urgency with no explanation and cannot correct a misclassification
evidence:
<StatusBadge tone={urgencyTone(grievance.urgency)} label={`${grievance.urgency} urgency`} />
<StatusBadge tone="neutral" label={grievance.category} />  -- no classification_reasoning/confidence; routes/api.php:426 only offers PATCH /grievances/{grievance}/status
impact: The SAO and the org Admin, who decide the case, see 'Critical urgency' as plain fact. Nothing marks it as a keyword-based suggestion or says why it was given; only the student's page has a 'Why this classification?' disclosure. A false Critical (see finding 05) cannot be lowered. It stays in the SAO's Critical tile, in the briefing's 'Urgent grievances unresolved' count and in Ask AI until the case is closed.
suggested_fix: In the drawer, label the badges 'Suggested urgency' and 'Suggested category' and render RulesDisclosure with classification_reasoning. Add PATCH /grievances/{grievance}/classification (SUPER_ADMIN, and the org ADMIN through canTransition) that validates urgency in Low/Medium/High/Critical and category in the known list, sets classification_engine='reviewer', and writes an audit row.
verifier_notes: GrievanceDetailDrawer renders urgency/category as plain badges with no classification_reasoning; only StudentGrievancesPage has the "Why this classification?" disclosure. routes/api.php offers only PATCH /grievances/{grievance}/status, so no reviewer correction path exists.

title: Classification reasoning names no keyword, so the 'Why this classification?' disclosure explains nothing
evidence: "reasoning": f"Determined {urgency} urgency and the '{matched_category}' category from keyword analysis."  (PHP mirror GrievanceController.php:351; shown in StudentGrievancesPage.jsx:42)
impact: A student who opens 'Why this classification?' reads the result again plus the phrase 'keyword analysis'. Nothing says which words set the urgency. When no keyword matched, the text still claims General came 'from keyword analysis'.
suggested_fix: Collect the matched keywords in both engines and phrase them plainly, for example 'Marked High because the text mentions "stole"; filed under Financial Integrity because it mentions "fund" and "receipt".' Use a separate sentence when nothing matched ('No urgent words were found, so it is Low and General until a reviewer looks at it'). Keep the Python and PHP output identical for the parity test.
verifier_notes: Both engines return the fixed sentence "Determined X urgency and the Y category from keyword analysis." with no matched keywords, including when nothing matched.

title: Negated keywords escalate grievances to Critical or High
evidence:
if any(_matches(text, keyword) for keyword in CRITICAL_KEYWORDS):
    urgency = "Critical"  -- I ran it: 'This is not an emergency, just a scheduling question' -> Critical, Safety & Security, 0.95
impact: A routine scheduling question is shown to the student and the SAO as Critical with 0.95 confidence. It inflates the SAO's Critical tile and the 'Urgent grievances unresolved' briefing item, and nobody can correct it (finding 03).
suggested_fix: Before the urgency match, drop a keyword hit that a negator ('not', 'no', 'hindi', 'dili', 'walang') precedes within two words, in both the Python and PHP engines. Add tests for 'not an emergency' and 'not urgent'.
verifier_notes: Reproduced: "This is not an emergency, just a scheduling question" -> Critical, Safety & Security, 0.95. "scheduling" also misses the whole-word "schedule" keyword.

title: Category ties go to Safety & Security by list order: 'theft of money' is not Financial Integrity
evidence: if matches > max_matches:  -- dict order puts Safety & Security first; 'theft' is only in Safety, 'money' only in Financial. I ran it: 'theft of money' -> category 'Safety & Security'
impact: Theft of organization money goes to Safety & Security rather than Financial Integrity, so SAO reviewers who filter by category miss financial cases.
suggested_fix: Add 'theft' to the Financial Integrity list. Or break ties by giving finance terms more weight than generic safety terms when a money word is present, then mirror the change in PHP and add a parity test case.
verifier_notes: Reproduced: "theft of money" -> High, Safety & Security. One match each; strict > keeps the first category in dict order (Safety).

title: SAO grievance table claims 'most urgent first' but sorts only the current page
evidence: const sortedRows = useMemo(() => { const copy = [...rows]; copy.sort(... urgencyRank ...) }, [rows, sort]);  caption="Grievances, most urgent first"  -- server: $query->orderByDesc('created_at')->orderByDesc('id')->paginate(...) (GrievanceController.php:83)
impact: With more than 50 grievances, an older Critical grievance sits on page 2 or later while page 1 opens with Low ones. The SAO's triage view hides the most urgent cases it is meant to put first.
suggested_fix: Add a validated 'sort' query parameter to GrievanceController::index (urgency: CASE urgency WHEN 'Critical' THEN 0 ... END, then created_at desc), pass the DataTable sort to the request, and drop the client-side re-sort.
verifier_notes: SaoGrievancesPage sorts only the 50 rows it fetched; index() orders by created_at desc and has no sort parameter, so page 1 is newest, not most urgent.

title: SAO 'Critical' tile counts resolved and dismissed grievances
impact: The Critical tile never goes down as cases are closed, which contradicts the comment that the tiles count the queue that needs a person. It also disagrees with the briefing's 'Urgent grievances unresolved' count, which excludes closed cases.
suggested_fix: Request the tile with status 'submitted,under_review' (FilterValues already accepts lists): getGrievances({ urgency: 'Critical', status: 'submitted,under_review', per_page: 1 }).
verifier_notes: The Critical tile requests urgency=Critical with no status filter, so resolved and dismissed Critical cases stay counted. FilterValues accepts comma lists for status.

title: SAO grievance tiles are never refreshed after a status change
evidence:
useEffect(() => { ... Promise.all([...TILE_STATUSES..., ...TILE_URGENCIES...]) ... }, []);
async function handleTransition(id, data) { ... load(); }
impact: After moving a grievance to Under review or Resolved, the table reloads but the Submitted and Under review tiles keep their old numbers until the page is reloaded.
suggested_fix: Move the tile fetch into a loadCounts callback and call it from handleTransition and onDeleted, as well as on mount.
verifier_notes: The tile effect runs once on mount ([] deps); handleTransition only calls load(), which reloads the table, not counts.

title: Ask AI grievance queue reports at most 12 unresolved and urgent grievances
impact: With 30 unresolved grievances, the SAO is told 'There are 12 unresolved grievance(s)', and the high or critical count is capped the same way. That understates the queue and contradicts the dashboard briefing's uncapped count.
suggested_fix: Compute the totals with separate count() queries (total unresolved, and unresolved with urgency High or Critical) before the limited row query. Use the limited collection only for the rows.
verifier_notes: buildGrievancesStatus takes counts from the limit(12) collection, so total is capped at 12 (urgent count is capped too once >12 urgent, since rows are ordered by urgency first). Additionally, DB::table bypasses SoftDeletes, so grievances a student deleted are still counted and listed.
corrected_fix: Run separate count() queries for total unresolved and High/Critical unresolved before the limited row query, and add ->whereNull('deleted_at') to all three queries (Grievance uses SoftDeletes and DB::table does not apply it).

title: Turnout-pace insight counts eligible voters differently from the voter roll it claims to reuse
evidence: $eligibleTotal = DB::table('users')->where('organization_id', $organizationId)->where('account_status', 'active')->whereIn('role', ['ADMIN', 'SBO_OFFICER', 'STUDENT'])->count();  // ElectionBallotController::voters uses AccountProfile::onVoterRoll(...)->where('account_profiles.organization_id', $organizationId) plus anyone who voted
impact: Members who belong to the organization only through an account profile are left out of the denominator. Profile-only voters still add ballots, so turnout can exceed 100%, or it can differ from the Manage Voters summary. The insight can then fire, or stay silent, when it should not, while its 'Why?' text says the formula is reused from the voter list.
suggested_fix: Extract the eligible and voted counting in ElectionBallotController::voters into a shared method, for example on Election or a VoterRollService, keyed on AccountProfile::onVoterRoll($election->finalized_at), and call it from electionTurnoutPace.
verifier_notes: electionTurnoutPace counts users.organization_id members with role in ADMIN/SBO_OFFICER/STUDENT; ElectionBallotController::voters counts account_profiles onVoterRoll(finalized_at) for the org plus anyone who voted. Profile-only members and finalized_at cut-off diverge; voted count includes ballots from profile-only voters, so turnout can exceed 100%.

title: Workload insight drops officers already at the task limit, hiding the overloaded officer
evidence:
})->filter(fn ($workload) => $workload['active_tasks'] < $maxActive)->values();
... 'body' => "{$busiest['name']} is carrying {$busiest['active_tasks']} active task(s) while ..."
impact: With two officers, one holding 9 active tasks (max 5) and one holding 0, the busy officer is filtered out and the insight returns null, so the worst imbalance never shows. With more officers, the 'busiest' named is the busiest one under the limit, not the one who is overloaded.
suggested_fix: Compute busiest over all eligible officers (min($active, $maxActive) already bounds the score). Pick freest only among officers under the limit, and state in the body when the busiest is at or over the limit.
verifier_notes: The filter active_tasks < maxActive removes overloaded officers before busiest is chosen; two officers at 9 and 0 leave one row and the insight returns null.

title: Officers get a workload suggestion naming peers' task loads that they cannot act on
evidence: 'insights' => array_slice($this->insightEngine->forOrganization($orgId, $role), 0, 3),  // includeTaskWorkload defaults true; href '/dashboard/tasks/task-board' is ADMIN-only in client_routes.php, and POST /tasks is role:ADMIN
impact: An SBO officer is told 'Consider assigning the next task to a less loaded officer', which names two colleagues and their active task counts, with no link. The officer has no permission to assign tasks. The card shares peer workload data with no action behind it.
suggested_fix: Call forOrganization($orgId, $role, includeTaskWorkload: false) in buildOfficer, or include the workload insight only when $role === 'ADMIN'.
verifier_notes: buildOfficer calls forOrganization($orgId, $role) with includeTaskWorkload defaulting true; /dashboard/tasks/task-board is only in the ADMIN list in client_routes.php, so href is null for SBO_OFFICER, and POST /tasks is role:ADMIN.

title: Forecast insight shows raw engine terms (r-squared, insufficient_data, deficit) to users
evidence:
'title' => "Financial forecast for {$period}: {$risk}",
'inputs' => ['sample_months' => ..., 'fit_quality' => $details['fit_quality'] ?? null, 'income_r_squared' => ..., 'expense_r_squared' => ...]
impact: Officers and admins see 'Financial forecast for December 2026: overspending'. Under 'Why?' they read 'fit quality (insufficient_data), income r squared (0.12)'. The engine's terms are passed through without any plain-language meaning.
suggested_fix: Map risk to plain titles ('Spending may outpace income in December 2026'). Replace the r-squared and fit_quality inputs with a plain reliability sentence ('Based on 4 months of records; the trend is weak, so treat this as a rough guide'), and drop null inputs.
verifier_notes: Title interpolates the raw risk value and inputs pass fit_quality and r_squared values straight through to the Why disclosure.

impact: UX_FLOW 4.9 makes the Admin the reviewer for grievances addressed to the organization. A Critical grievance waiting on the Admin appears only as a bell notice and never in 'Needs attention'.

title: Grievance notification links drop the record id, so the drawer does not open
evidence: grievance: (role) => pick({ SUPER_ADMIN: '/dashboard/super-admin/grievances', ADMIN: '/dashboard/grievances', STUDENT: '/dashboard/my-grievances' }, role),  // pages support ?record= via useGrievanceRecord
impact: Tapping 'New grievance filed' or 'Your grievance was updated' lands on the list, not the grievance. The reviewer has to hunt for it, which is slow when the queue is long and the list is sorted by date.
suggested_fix: Take the id and wrap each path with record(path, id), matching the other destinations. ClientRouteAccess and the client already allow 'record'.
verifier_notes: Real for SUPER_ADMIN and ADMIN: SaoGrievancesPage and OrganizationGrievancesPage use useGrievanceRecord, which reads ?record= and fetches the grievance. Wrong for STUDENT: StudentGrievancesPage does not use useGrievanceRecord, so a record param there does nothing. notificationLinks.test.js pins the current paths.
corrected_fix: Take the id in the grievance destination and wrap only the SUPER_ADMIN and ADMIN paths with record(path, id) (or also add ?record= support to StudentGrievancesPage before wrapping its path); update the grievance expectations in notificationLinks.test.js.

title: Template fallback drafts use up the daily AI announcement quota
evidence: $used = AiOutput::query()->where('organization_id', ...)->where('requested_by', ...)->where('feature_type', 'ANNOUNCEMENT_DRAFT')->whereDate('created_at', now()->toDateString())->count();  // generateDraft stores model_name 'template-draft' rows under the same feature_type
impact: While the AI writer is down, each attempt returns the canned template and still counts against the 20-a-day limit. When the service recovers, the officer may already be blocked with 'You have used all announcement drafts available today'.
suggested_fix: Exclude template rows from the quota count: ->where('model_name', '!=', 'template-draft'), or ->where('context_version', '!=', 'announcement-template-v1').
verifier_notes: Behaviour is real: template rows are stored under feature_type ANNOUNCEMENT_DRAFT with requested_by = school_id and counted by the quota. But it is pinned by test_groq_failure_returns_a_template_draft_labelled_as_such (asserts quota.remaining 19 after a template), so it looks deliberate; the defect is a design choice rather than an oversight, and the fix must change that test.
corrected_fix: Exclude rows with context_version = announcement-template-v1 from announcementGenerationQuota and update AnnouncementAiWorkflowTest::test_groq_failure_returns_a_template_draft_labelled_as_such to expect quota.remaining 20.

title: University insights are computed for SAO and Department Head but never shown
evidence: const showInsights = role !== 'SUPER_ADMIN' && role !== 'DEPARTMENT_HEAD';  // server still runs forUniversity(...) in buildSuperAdmin (DashboardBriefingService.php:248) and buildDepartmentHead (:181)
impact: Every SAO and Department Head home load runs a distinct-count query over all budgets whose result the client throws away. The server contract and the client also disagree about which roles get insights.
suggested_fix: Return 'insights' => [] for SUPER_ADMIN and DEPARTMENT_HEAD in DashboardBriefingService, and remove forUniversity if nothing else uses it. Or show the insights for those roles if that is intended.
